doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Monk Competition, joining Jason Mraz, and commuting to New York
summary: The Monk Competition showed him the wider scene; after Maynard's death he joined Jason Mraz and visited New York monthly while caring about his aging father.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: became aware of what else existed out there. Andre Hayward won that competition. I met — re-connected with Andre there, re-connected with Steve Davis, Elliot Mason was a competitor, Marshall Gilkes, all these great trombone players. And the judges of course: Grachan Moncur, Julian Priester, Steve Davis, Curtis Fuller, you know. And then of course Herbie Hancock is there, Wayne Shorter is there, all the Monk Institute people. So that was a time for me when I thought wow this is, now I’m getting a view of what’s really going on you know. I didn’t feel like I belonged there at all but that was the first sense I got for what was happening. After Maynard died, two years after that I got the call to go with Jason Mraz, and that was something I couldn’t turn down. And that lasted a long time. And also New York, I kind of missed my opportunity — my father lived to be 92 and as he was aging I thought it’s bad enough I’m on the road, I want to go home and check on him, and I didn’t want to disappear from the region completely so just choices were made and that time between 2006 and 2008 I would — you can ask my wife, I would go to New York once a month on a bus and sleep on my friend’s couch, go to sessions and hang out, yeah.
